exposure: comorbid Type-2 diseases (asthma, allergic rhinitis, food allergy)
outcome: Presence and prevalence of autoreactive IgE autoantibodies
cohort: Serum samples were collected from 672 participants aged 1.2 to 88.9 years, including patients with Atopic Dermatitis (sub-grouped by presence of Type-2 diseases), atopic controls without AD but with Type-2 diseases, and non-atopic healthy controls.
finding: IgE autoantibodies were found in 15.0% of AD patients, with a higher prevalence in those with comorbid Type-2 diseases (16.4%), and their development was associated with younger age, higher total serum IgE levels, birth between January and June, cesarean-section, and diversity of domestic pets.
mod_finding: Cesarean-section was identified as a factor affecting IgE autoantibody development.
cross-section timing: Observations were taken at a single point in time for each participant, across a wide age range from 1.2 to 88.9 years.
